items.prompt: A fictional policy brief calls an announced allowance universal because its legal scope is broad. It counts only completed payments, ignores late payments and unavailable appointments, and recommends expansion without defining the problem or responsible actors. Give five corrections.
items.model_answer: Define the problem, intended population and policy actors; distinguish legal entitlement from effective receipt; examine regularity and adequacy against purpose; identify complementary service and access conditions; and recommend a bounded evidence check through an authorised role. Do not determine real eligibility or infer universal reach from a payment count.

items.prompt: An invented budget approves 120 units and records 90 spent for a comparable period. A portal posts an undated image, six recommendations are issued, and publicity claims proven theft of 30 units and six completed service improvements. Give five corrections.
items.model_answer: Calculate the 30-unit difference and 75 percent spending proportion; seek comparable scope, versions and a reconciliation without alleging theft; distinguish expenditure from service delivery; require usable disclosure and a responsible explanation route; and distinguish recommendations, implemented action and evidenced outcomes with attribution limits.

items.prompt: A fictional decentralised desk is responsible for hours and materials but controls neither. It offers only an inaccessible form, treats sending a referral as resolution and reports a coordination meeting as universal access. Give five corrections.
items.model_answer: Map actual decisions and resources rather than infer powers from a label; identify the responsibility mismatch and authorised clarification role; propose a staffed accessible alternative with understandable reasons; confirm receiving responsibility and follow-up; and distinguish coordination activity from evidenced service outcomes. Do not invent constitutional or statutory powers.

items.prompt: Develop a conditional reform brief across all eight SPG courses for an invented social-support service. Legal scope is called universal receipt; an approved budget is called delivered support; a digital portal has no response owner; a district desk lacks resources and decision powers; consultation promises influence over closed choices; and a before-and-after count is called proof of impact. Explain the problem, actors, distribution, options, delivery sequence, evidence limits and accountable review. Use fictional records only.
items.model_answer: Integrate policy problem definition, actors, evidence, equity and feasible recommendations (028); entitlement, effective coverage, adequacy and complementary services (071); comparable allocations, execution, usable disclosure and follow-up (072); mechanisms, assumptions, resources, versioned adaptation and evaluation (073); actual institutional authority, inclusive access and traceable coordination (074); distribution, incentives and bounded study comparisons without motive allegations (075); honest scope, accessible input, missing perspectives and reasoned feedback (076); and a concise claim record, options comparison, staged decision and review plan (077). Name authorised decision roles, unresolved resources and observations that would change the recommendation. No classroom output approves expenditure, eligibility or an audit.

items.prompt: Critique a fictional claim that a downloaded policy brief has completed a nationally effective reform. The brief compares a US randomised transfer study with a Brazilian cohort as a universal policy ranking, treats Nigerian digital-budget propositions as proven corruption reduction, calls equal payments equal access, treats a coordination meeting as resolved referrals and consultation volume as universal consent, and promises certification from reading slides. Use all eight SPG domains to correct the claim and specify a proportionate next phase.
items.model_answer: Separate policy intent from implementation and effects (028); coverage, regularity and adequacy from nominal provision (071); budgets and recommendations from delivery and outcomes (072); process counts, denominators, changing targets and concurrent influences from causal claims (073); institutional labels and sent referrals from actual authority and responses (074); contextual distribution, incentives and design-specific research limits from universal rankings (075); honest influence and feedback from repeated submissions or inferred consent (076); and accepted briefs or downloads from implemented, evaluated reform (077). Propose a verified, resourced and reviewable next step with clear evidence limits. Reading alone earns no badge or certificate: verified course CBT passes, the configured mixed ParaLearn school exam, criterion-level human marking, independent moderation and authorised signatures remain required.
